source.name: Diverclaim/UnderrailMods
source.license_note: No license file was present in the reviewed repository snapshot; this project summarizes concepts and links to the source, but does not vendor code.

scope_note: Runtime IL / assembly quality-of-life patches, not global.dat save edits. Stable patches are exposed only in the separate Runtime Mods expert tab with scan, dry-run, backup, and rollback controls; no game assets or third-party code are vendored.

mods.name: Fastforward
mods.effect: Temporarily increases game speed while a hotkey is held.
mods.integration_signal: Requires hooking GameTime assignment and routing through a Mods.ApplyFastforward-style helper.

mods.name: Item weight
mods.effect: Applies a multiplier to item weight calculations so the player can carry more.
mods.integration_signal: Targets SingleItemWeight and Weight property getters; safer as a runtime DLL/assembly patch than a save mutation.
mods.default_in_this_tool: weight multiplier 0.1 after live testing; 0.001 was too close to zero for practical play

mods.name: Traders buy all
mods.effect: Makes traders accept all item types and quantities.
mods.integration_signal: Targets barter UI acceptance checks and text explaining what a trader wants to buy.

mods.name: Force restock
mods.effect: Forces merchant inventory restock, triggered by holding a hotkey while selecting the Barter dialog option.
mods.integration_signal: Targets the merchant restock method and toggles the boolean restock argument before original logic executes.

mods.name: Throwing hit chance cap
mods.effect: Changes the hard cap used in throwing hit chance calculations.
mods.integration_signal: Targets repeated 0.9 clamp constants in the throwing chance array calculation.

design_implications: Separate save-file respecs from runtime IL/assembly mods; they have different risk, versioning, and legal/support models.
A future mod system should use a manifest/catalog with explicit target type, game-version compatibility, default settings, and rollback instructions.
Runtime patches need obfuscation-tolerant matching by semantic anchors such as property names, interface attribute strings, UI text, and constant clusters.
The current clone-first save editor should not modify game binaries or DLLs without a separate explicit expert workflow.
